And the wretched man remained {OCR?} for some time,
and died.
And they say
that he believed in Christ again,
and died a Christian.
And from Edessa the Sultan went to Qal'at Ja'bar,
and there was a band of brigands there.
And when they went out to fight with the Turks,
three of the Turks scaled the wall from the other side,
where no one thought that there was a place to climb,
and they cried out in the name of the Sultan.
And those brigands, when they heard the voice, were terrified,
and their hands grew slack.
And the Turks captured them,
and killed Ja'bar, their chief.
Now the wife of this man was a courageous woman,
and she cast herself down from the wall;
and the wind got into her cloak and gently brought her down to the ground,
and she was not harmed.
And when they brought her to the Sultan, and he asked her,
"Why did you do this?", she answered:
"Because I chose to die,
rather than that any other man besides my husband should have power over me."
And he asked her from where she was, and she said,
"From Damascus."
And the Sultan commanded,
and they mounted her and conducted her to her people.
And from there the Sultan went to Aleppo and to Antioch,
and gained dominion over them.
And he turned back and came to Baghdad on account of the dearness and famine that were in Syria,
and he gave his daughter to the Caliph in marriage.
And from there he went to Khorasan.
And over Edessa and Melitene was appointed head the Emir Buzan,
and over Aleppo, Aq Sunqur (Agh Sunqur?).
And in the year 485
485 of the Arabs [1092 AD],
the Sultan came from Khorasan to Baghdad.
And there was a dispute between him and the Caliph,
because he demanded of the Caliph
that he proclaim as Caliph after him his son who was born of the Sultan's daughter.
And when the Caliph declined,
the Sultan sent word to him:
"Depart then from Baghdad."
And the Caliph replied:
"I will fulfill your command,
only bear with me for ten days,
until I prepare for departure."
And on the ninth day,
the Sultan contracted a burning inflammatory fever,
and died.
And it is said
that Kurdik his slave gave him poison to drink.
Now Terken Khatun, his wife,
because she was a prudent woman,
she herself took control of the affairs of the kingdom.
